preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
The following clinical scenario applies to the following 2 questions:

Susan is a 23-year-old healthy female who is visiting her family physician for a prenatal session.

She and her partner, Mike, a 25- year- old healthy gentleman, are planning a pregnancy.

Susan and Mike are concerned as Mike recently found out that his paternal uncle died many

years ago because of cardiac complications secondary to Deschene Muscular Dystrophy.

According to Mike the diagnosis was clinical based on high CK levels and calf

pseudohypertrophy. Genetic testing was not an option at that time. Mike’s father has no other

siblings and has been healthy all his life.

preamble.html: The case. A 44 yo physician developed the sudden onset of seeing flashes of light on the right hand side while studying. She does her own exam and finds that she has distorted vision in both right sides of her vision, when she closes either eye. It lasts about 20 minutes and then resolves. preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 75 year old man starts having difficulty with speaking. Initially, his family noted 2 months ago that he had difficulty recalling the names of familiar objects. Then one month ago, he started using the wrong word for things. Over the last week, his sentences have not been making any sense to his family members. His exam shows a slight right facial droop, reduced inability to name objects, difficulty with repetition, but he could follow commands. Reflexes normal.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 68 yo woman complains of progressive difficulty walking over the past 3 weeks. She has fallen a couple of times. She has also notices that her hands are not as coordinated as she had been previously. She is urinating more frequently and with greater urgency. Exam shows: subtle weakness of her hip flexion bilaterally but otherwise full strength. She has very brisk reflexes in her arms and her legs, and both toes are upgoing. Vibration sensation is impaired significantly at both great toes. Her gait is wide based and unsteady.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
THE FOLLOWING QUESTION STEM APPLIES TO THE NEXT TWO QUESTIONS!

You are a physician seeing a new patient, Alice. Alice is 84 years old and states that she feels

well today. Her husband passed away three years ago. She drove to the clinic today and you

noticed a sizeable dent in her car when entering the clinic. She claims that she was side-swiped

in city traffic last month. She scored [24+1] on the MoCA when completed today, losing most of

her points in the serial sevens. Her vision and hearing were recently tested and no abnormalities

were identified.

She complains of fatigue at times and the occasional headrush when standing up quickly. Past-

medical history includes three instances of post-partum depression (PPD) and has been pregnant

six times. Current medication includes over-the-counter calcium supplements (500mg) and

physician-prescribed antipsychotic sleeping pills (Seroquel, an antipsychotic), without which she

cannot fall asleep. When you question her about her ADLs and IADLs, she is mostly

independent but requires help with finances from her adult son ever since the passing of her

husband, who primarily took care of finances. She seems peppy during your interview and she

relates that her greatest pleasure is spending time with her great- grandchildren, who are 3 and 7.

She watches them during the week while her grandchildren work full- time jobs.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 25-year-old male patient presents with several enlarged lymph nodes in the supraclavicular region. The patient remarked feeling easily fatigued, with mild shortness of breath upon physical activity, and bloating. He denied fever, weight loss or night sweats. An excisional biopsy reveals the patient has Hodgkin Lymphoma. Subsequent PET-CT scans indicate that the lymphoma is limited to his supraclavicular lymph nodes, axillary lymph nodes, a small mediastinal mass, and abdominal lymph nodes.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 60-year-old woman presents to her family doctor with swollen and painful joints in her hands and feet for the last 8 weeks. Her past medical history is significant for high blood pressure, gallstones and periodontal disease. She smokes a pack of cigarettes a day for the last 40 years and denies any illicit drug use. She drinks 2 alcoholic beverages a day. She has a family history of rheumatoid arthritis in her mother and cousin and heart disease in her father and brother.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html:
The case. A 60-year-old woman presents to her family doctor with swollen and painful joints in her hands and feet for the last 8 weeks. Her past medical history is significant for high blood pressure, gallstones and periodontal disease. She smokes a pack of cigarettes a day for the last 40 years and denies any illicit drug use. She drinks 2 alcoholic beverages a day. She has a family history of rheumatoid arthritis in her mother and cousin and heart disease in her father and brother.

The family doctor examined the patient and felt that there was swelling in the patient’s wrists and the small joints of the hand and feet. The history, physical exam findings and presence of several risk factors for RA made the doctor concerned for a diagnosis of RA and the patient was referred to rheumatology. When the patient saw rheumatology, labs were sent for anti-citrullinated protein/peptide antibodies (ACPA) that were positive. In patients presenting with inflammatory arthritis, ACPA is very specific for RA. The patient was diagnosed with RA.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A two-month-old female infant presents with protracted diarrhea leading to severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance. A positive stool culture for the opportunistic protozoan Cryptosporidium parvum is reported, and the patient is referred to you for immunological evaluation. You find subnormal levels of IgG and IgA in the serum. Flow cytometric analyses of the patient’s peripheral blood indicate that CD19+CD20+ cells (B cells) and CD14+ cells (monocytes) are within the normal range. However, HLA class II molecules are missing on the surface of these cells. In addition, a decreased frequency of CD3+ cells (T cells) are found. Your diagnosis is bare lymphocyte syndrome (BLS) type II. You explain to the parents the possibility of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation as a potential (although not necessarily perfect) treatment option.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
Use the following clinical scenario to answer the next THREE questions.

Sarah Hyland is an American actress who played Haley Dunphy in the comedy TV show,

Modern Family. In 2012, her kidneys failed due to a congenital condition known as kidney

dysplasia. Her father stepped up and became a living donor. Then, in 2016, her body began to

reject her father’s kidney. In 2017, she started regular hemodialysis treatments, three times per

week, each lasting 4 hours. In 2018, she received an organ transplant from her brother.
